Velut et al. 2017 outward-striking one-mass lip model: h'' + (w_l/Q_l) h' + w_l^2 (h - h0) = (p_b - p(t))/mu (eq. 1), Bernoulli flow u = W h sqrt(2(p_b - p)/rho) (eq. 5), impedance as sum of complex modes Z(w) = Zc sum_n [C_n/(jw - s_n) + C_n*/(jw - s_n*)] (eq. 3), with modal ODEs dp_n/dt = Zc C_n u + s_n p_n and p = 2 sum Re(p_n) (eq. 4).
Velut et al. 2017 lip parameters (Table 2): h0 = 5e-4 m, W = 12e-3 m, 1/mu = 0.11 m^2/kg (mu ~ 9.1 kg/m^2), Q_l = 7, with f_l swept 20-500 Hz; rho = 1.19 kg/m^3.

Freour et al. 2020 trumpet parameter set (same one-mass outward model, eq. 1-6): Q_l = 3, mu_l = 2 kg/m^2, y0 = 0.1 mm, b = 8 mm (eq. 15), with f_l = 382.18 Hz chosen by LSA 'sweet spot' so that the 4th regime (Bb4, ~470 Hz) is played; Hopf bifurcation at p0 ~ 2.2 kPa.

Doc, Vergez & Hannebicq 2023 give a register-by-register trumpet lip parameter set (L = 12 mm, Q_l = 20, mu = 9 kg/m^2) that makes the one-mass outward model play registers 2-6 in time-domain synthesis: p_b = 1256/2146/2973/3790/4931 Pa, f_l = 235/340/467/586/703 Hz, h0 = 0.242/0.218/0.190/0.172/0.168 mm.

Berjamin et al. (2017) trumpet-like simulation uses a one-mass lip m y'' + r y' + k(y - y_eq) = A (p_m - p_e) with m = 1.78e-4 kg, k = 1278.8 N/m, r = sqrt(mk)/4 (i.e. Q = 4, f_l ~ 427 Hz), lip width l = 1e-2 m, A = 1e-4 m^2, y_eq = 5e-4 m, p_m = 20 kPa.

Bilbao/NESS-style FDTD lip parameter set (as tabulated in Willemsen, Bilbao, Ducceschi, Serafin, DAFx20in21, citing Harrison-Harsley 2018 thesis): M_r = 5.37e-5 kg, S_r = 1.46e-5 m^2, sigma_r = 5 s^-1, w_r = 0.01 m, H0 = 2.9e-4 m, omega_r/2pi 20-1000 Hz, P_m 0-6000 Pa (trombone context).

The planner's lip simulator (research/spikes/lipsim.cpp: Freour 2022 eq. 1, bilinear modal update at 96 kHz, closed-form implicit flow) reproduces Freour et al. 2022: with their Table 1 open-trumpet modes and Table 2 lips (Ql 3, mu 2 kg/m^2, y0 0.1 mm, b 8 mm) at f_l = 382.18 Hz it oscillates at f0 = 479.7 Hz for p0 = 3 kPa (paper: ~470 Hz, Hopf ~2.2 kPa) and does not start from rest at 2.0 kPa.

With the bell filter applied as a linear (zero-padded) convolution, the 'tongue release' attack gives onset medians of 40-160 ms by the reference metric (TinySOL band q10-q90: pp 26-164, mf 22-103, ff 22-99 ms); the best single setting (pressure rise 15 ms, lips closed, accent 1.5) puts 92/58/25 % of pp/mf/ff notes inside the band, and dynamic-dependent settings reach >= 50 % for every dynamic (pp 92 % at 15 ms/closed, mf 58 % at 15 ms/closed/accent 1.5, ff 50 % at 15 ms/half-open); >= 80 % per dynamic was not reached. Supersedes C-088 (circular-convolution artefact, lesson L-20261008T010500Z).

A 25 ms tongue stop (lips held closed, p_m = 0, then a 3 ms pressure re-attack) on a sustained mf note gives a 5 ms-RMS dip of 11.7-20.1 dB (median 15.9) in the radiated output of every normal-range standard note and recovery to within 3 dB of the steady level in a median 95 ms (97 % within 250 ms); 15 ms gives 7.7-16.8 dB; a 100 ms gap gives >= 29 dB.

After the D-007 release (p_m to 0 over 40 ms) the radiated output of every normal-range standard note at mf falls by 16.9-56.4 dB (median 38.8) below its steady level within 100 ms of note-off; only 87 % fall by >= 20 dB.

Lossless weakly nonlinear simple-wave propagation used for brassiness: dp/dt + [c0 + ((gamma+1)/2) u] dp/dx = 0 (eq. 1), which with p = rho0 c0 u and retarded time tau = t - x/c0 becomes dp/dx - ((gamma+1)/(2 rho0 c0^3)) p dp/dtau = 0 (eq. 2); for a flaring bore D(x) add + p (1/D) dD/dx (eq. 5), removed by the stretched coordinate z(x) = int_0^x D0/D(y) dy and w = D p (eqs. 6-8).

Shock formation distance: x_s = 2 gamma P_at c / ((gamma+1)(dp_m/dt)_max) (Hirschberg et al. eq. 1), equivalently x_s = rho0 c0^3 / (beta (dp/dt)_max) with beta = (gamma+1)/2 = 1.2; for a sinusoid of amplitude P, (dp/dt)_max = 2 pi f P, giving e.g. 2.76 m at 466 Hz/5 kPa, 1.38 m at 466 Hz/10 kPa, 0.69 m at 466 Hz/20 kPa (rho0 = 1.2, c0 = 343 m/s).

Effective nonlinear (equivalent-cylinder) length of a modern B-flat trumpet: brassiness potential B = (1/L_ecN) int_0^L Dmin/D(x) dx = 0.58 with Dmin = 8.7 mm for a Yamaha trumpet (c. 2002), i.e. L_NDeq = B x L_ecN ~ 0.85 m of 8.7 mm tube (L_ecN = c/(2 f1) ~ 1.47 m); a 19th-century Kessler trumpet has B = 0.74; the OpenWInD Tr_co_MP bore gives B ~ 0.61 (Dmin 9.28 mm, z(L) = 0.90 m).

Real-time algorithm options: Vergez & Rodet 2000 (J. Signal Processing 4(1):79-87) proposed a new algorithm for nonlinear propagation applied to a trumpet model, Msallam et al. 2000 (Acta Acust. 86(4):725-736) a trombone model with nonlinear propagation in the cylindrical part, and Helie & Smet 2008 a real-time 'brassy' audio effect for a straight pipe; none of these full texts were accessible, so the algorithm details below are derived from eq. (2) and not from them.

Output chain p+ = p/2 -> simple-wave time warping over 0.85 m of equivalent cylinder -> TMM bell transfer j w H / Z_rad gives a mean harmonic MAD (H1..H8) vs TinySOL of 2.9 dB at ff (6 notes), but pp/mf are too bright (13.6 / 7.5 dB) when the steady pressure stays at 1.3 / 2.5 x threshold; without nonlinear propagation ff is too dark (centroid ratio 0.47-0.59).

A one-mass outward-striking model CAN produce a pedal-like note well above the strongly inharmonic first resonance: for the trombone Velut et al. find f_thresh,1 = 55.6 Hz vs f_ac,1 = 38 Hz (ratio 1.46, close to Bb1 = 58.27 Hz) at f_l = 49 Hz, and time-domain simulation at p_b = 150 Pa gives 61.86 Hz; a single-mode resonator still gives 61.06 Hz, so the pedal is attributed to coupling with the first mode, not the privileged-frequency mechanism of upper modes.

For the outward-striking one-mass model the playing (threshold) frequency is always just ABOVE the acoustic resonance f_ac,n, and the least-threshold ('optimal') lip frequency lies slightly BELOW it: trombone Table 5 gives f_l,opt/f_ac,n = 110/112 = 0.98, 162/170 = 0.95, 215/228 = 0.94, 271/290 = 0.93 for regimes 2-5, with f_thresh/f_ac,n = 1.10, 1.06, 1.05, 1.04 (Q_l = 7).

With trumpet parameters of low Q_l the optimal lip frequency is much further below the resonance: Freour et al. 2020 find f_l = 382.18 Hz for the 4th resonance at 462.98 Hz (ratio 0.825, Q_l = 3), playing near 470 Hz; across 8 trumpets f_l/f_4 = 0.81-0.82.

Hysteresis: with Freour's trumpet parameters the Bb4 branch emerges from an inverse (subcritical) Hopf bifurcation at p0 ~ 2.2 kPa with a fold at lower p0, so sound starts at 2.2 kPa but can be sustained below it on decrescendo; across 8 trumpets the hysteresis width H = 0.25-0.59 kPa and the dynamic range D (p-p up to p0 = 5 kPa) = 8.4-9.8 kPa.

Overblow by continuous interpolation of the lip setting between partials (f_l, h0 and/or p_m) produces silent gaps > 50 ms between registers for 10-19 of 35 notes and non-monotonic partial sequences, so it is rejected.

Within a register, raising only the blowing pressure (p_m x (1 + 2 o) for o in [0, 0.45]) keeps 35/35 standard notes on their partial and increases the mouthpiece-pressure centroid monotonically for 35/35; adding f_l x (1 + 0.04 o) pushes 11/35 notes to the next partial early.

Over 4 s runs (R5 review) the Doc 2023 lip set with pressure k x threshold (pp 1.3, mf 2.5, ff 5) sustains standard notes written 54-85 at pp/mf/ff, 86-87 at mf/ff only, 88 at ff only, 89 at mf/ff only (86/87 at pp are ring-downs of the attack transient); with blowing-factor floors (86, 87, 89 >= 2.5; 88 >= 5.0, D-023) all four sustain for 3 s.

The per-note frequency scale holds pp/mf/ff within +-4.6 cents only by construction: it shifts all poles and f_l by up to -84 cents (standard notes) and -114 cents (alternates), so at Intonation realism = 0 it overrides the bore's natural tendencies; pitch values reported for non-sustaining notes (87 pp, 89 pp) are invalid.

In the Void Choir reference recording, harmonic levels are tied to absolute frequency (a fixed cabinet), not harmonic number: the RMS level difference between pitches is 5.9 dB aligned by Hz versus 10.5 dB aligned by harmonic number. A pre-clip lowpass whose cutoff scales with f0, with the high-pass moved after the clipper, made the clipper output's harmonic balance pitch-invariant (spread 10.1/6.2 dB -> 0.8/0.1 dB, lead/rhythm).

A cabinet response tabulated as dB against log frequency can be turned into a minimum-phase FIR at the AudioContext's own sample rate with the real-cepstrum method (log magnitude -> inverse FFT -> fold the cepstrum -> FFT -> exp -> inverse FFT). With N=8192 and 2048 taps it matched the table within 3 dB at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz, with at least 95% of its energy in the first 512 taps.

To compare harmonic levels of a voice with two oscillators detuned by c cents, analyse exactly one beat period, 1/(f0*(2^(c/1200)-1)), with a rectangular window, so every beat phase is weighted equally. For a 10-cent saw pair this reduced a spurious 12.7 dB cross-pitch spread to 0.1 dB, whereas Hann windows and multi-window averages still left 5-8 dB.

The demucs-onnx htdemucs export takes input 'mix' (1, 2, 343980) float32 at 44.1 kHz and returns 'stems' (1, 4, 2, 343980) in the order drums, bass, other, vocals; it is run on chunks of 343,980 samples with 25% overlap (stride 257,985), joined by triangular-window overlap-add with weight normalisation; the window is exactly 0 at index 0, so the first sample of a track is exactly 0 in every stem, and the four stems are not constrained to sum to the input.

A Hertzian impact force pulse is a half-sine to the power 3/2, sin^(3/2), with duration T = 2.943 delta_max / v (delta_max the peak indentation, v the impact speed); with delta_max = (5 m v^2 / (4 k))^(2/5) and k = (4/3) E* sqrt(R) this equals T = 2.868 (m^2 / (R E*^2 v))^(1/5), and the two forms agree to 6 digits in a numerical check (7.5329e-5 s for m = 0.05 kg, R = 10 mm, E* = 100 GPa, v = 2 m/s).

The driving-point impedance of an infinite thin plate is Z = 8 sqrt(D rho h), about 138 N s/m for 1.2 mm steel (E 200 GPa, nu 0.3, rho 7850 kg/m^3), independent of frequency; the arithmetic gives 138.13 N s/m.

The eigenvalues lambda of a clamped circular plate satisfy J_n(lambda) I_{n+1}(lambda) + I_n(lambda) J_{n+1}(lambda) = 0 with frequency proportional to lambda^2; the ideal ratio of the second axisymmetric mode (n=0, one nodal circle) to the fundamental is 3.893, the ratio (1,2) is 11.754 (the plan's 13.00 was wrong), and the computed lambda^2 values agree with the Manu et al. 2023 table to a worst relative error of 3.69e-7 over 42 values.

The oildrumkit engine maps plate mode ratios with r' = 1 + s(r - 1) and defaults to s = 0.8; only the lower anchor s = 0.57 (from the patent's 2.5-2.8 second-axisymmetric ratio: (2.65 - 1)/(3.893 - 1)) is supported by a source, the upper anchor s = 1.04 depended on the unsupported 4.0 ratio, so 0.8 is an engineering choice, not a measured value.

The ANSYS verification case VM-LSDYNA-SOLVE-051 (after Blevins 1979, Formulas for Natural Frequency and Mode Shape, table 11-1 case 3) lists a clamped circular plate (R 17 in, h 0.5 in, E 3e7 psi, rho 7.3e-4 lbf s^2/in^4, nu 0.3) with frequencies 172.64, 671.79 and 1505.07 Hz; the plate solver in oildrumkit gives 172.56 Hz for the fundamental, 0.05 % low; the id VM181 in the research note is wrong.

Circular cross-correlation is linear in its first operand (correlate(A+B, T) = correlate(A, T) + correlate(B, T)), and circularly rotating one operand by k rotates the correlation output by k: correlate(roll(T0, k), template)[b] = correlate(T0, template)[(b - k) mod B]. For Milne/Harrison-Pearce pitch-class harmonicity scored over many integer-cent candidates against the same held notes, this means the full per-candidate correlation vector can be obtained by precomputing two length-B vectors once (correlate(heldSpectrum, template) and correlate(noteSpectrumAtZero, template)) and combining them with an O(1) index shift per candidate, with no per-candidate FFT at all.

For the trumpet the bell radiation resistance rises as the square of frequency up to a radiation cut-off at about 1000 Hz, above which the bell radiates efficiently and reflects little, so the mouthpiece-to-radiated-pressure transfer function is a high-pass shape that rises with frequency up to ~1-1.5 kHz and is roughly flat above.

Third-valve slide (ring/saddle/trigger): push it out about 1/2 inch for 1-3 (D4, G3) and about 1 inch for 1-2-3 (C#4, F#3); on many horns G3 and F#3 are already low so only D4 and C#4 need correcting; the fix must arrive and leave with the note.

First-valve slide (thumb trigger/throw): lowers notes using valve 1 alone or 1-2, 1-3, 1-2-3 - Buckner names fifth-line F (F5), high A (A5) and high B-flat as sharp notes it corrects; Spang's chart prints 'USE 1st VALVE SLIDE' on A3, E4, A4, F5 and A5 (the 1-2 notes plus F5), and 'USE 3rd VALVE SLIDE' on G3, D4, C#4 and F#3; on low F3/E3 both.

Intonation reason: valve tubes are cut for the open horn, so a combination adds tubing computed on the unlengthened tube; the real second valve adds length to an already lengthened tube, so combinations come out short = sharp; the third slide cannot be tuned for everything, so design is a compromise (1 and 2 slightly flat, 3 alone very flat, to make combinations less sharp).
Valve lowerings: 2nd valve = 1 semitone (minor 2nd), 1st = 2 semitones (major 2nd), 3rd = 3 semitones (minor 3rd); 1-2 (or 3) = 3, 2-3 = 4, 1-3 = 5, 1-2-3 = 6 semitones (Arban row labels).

Typical cent deviations of combinations on real horns (Weidner): 2 -5c, 1 -5c, 1-2 +1c, 3 -21c, 2-3 -8c, 1-3 +7c, 1-2-3 +28c; school method (AmericanFork p.114): 1-2 moderately sharp, 2-3 moderately flat, 1-3 very sharp, 1-2-3 extremely sharp.

On node-web-audio-api 2.2.0, a DynamicsCompressorNode delays an impulse by 8.71 ms at 44.1 kHz, both at default settings and at threshold -6 dB, ratio 20, attack 1 ms; a GainNode adds 0 ms. A compressor on one of several parallel paths therefore shifts that path late.

A DynamicsCompressorNode at threshold -6 dB, ratio 20, attack 1 ms, knee 0 is not a peak ceiling: a sine at +6 dBFS came out at +0.09 dBFS on node-web-audio-api 2.2.0. A bounded ceiling needs a clipper (for example a tanh WaveShaper) after it.

AudioParam.exponentialRampToValueAtTime follows v(t) = V0 * (V1/V0)^((t-T0)/(T1-T0)) with V0 and V1 positive (a target of 0 throws), so ramping to 0.001 * V0 at T0 + 3d is an exponential decay with time constant 3d/ln(1000) = 0.434d; a per-sample multiplier exp(-1/(d*sr)) has time constant d, so the ramp decays 2.3 times faster, and at t = d the ramp is at 0.100 of its start against 0.368.
